anchor: closeted there, as it were, in the cabin
note: Closeted: shut up in a private room for a talk.
Intimations: hints. Billy cannot sense hidden danger easily.
The coxswain steered the captain’s boat and was a trusted sailor.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Coxswain”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Without: outside. The sentry is to stand outside the door.

anchor: an asylum-physician approaching in the public hall some patient
note: Asylum: a hospital for the insane. Paroxysm: a sudden attack of violent symptoms.

anchor: mesmerically looking him in the eye
note: Mesmerically: in a hypnotic way, as if to cast a spell.
Recapitulated: repeated in brief, summed up once more.
Leprosy is a disease that leaves white patches on the skin.

anchor: He stood like one impaled and gagged
note: Impaled: pierced through with a stake. Billy is frozen and silenced.
Dilated: widened with shock or fear.

anchor: gelidly protruding like the alien eyes
note: Gelidly: coldly, like jelly or ice. Protruding: bulging out.
Uncatalogued: not yet described by science.
Fascination: the power to hold someone spellbound. Snakes were thought to charm their prey.

anchor: the hungry lurch of the torpedo-fish
note: The torpedo-fish, or electric ray, shocks its prey with electricity.
Nonage: youth, the time before one is of full age.
Tongue-tie: loss of the power to speak. Convulsed: shaken.

anchor: a condemned Vestal priestess in the moment of being buried alive
note: In ancient Rome the Vestal priestesses served Vesta, goddess of the hearth. A Vestal who broke her vow of chastity was buried alive.
Impediment: something that hinders, here a stutter.

anchor: by much the same startling impotence
note: Impotence: helplessness, being unable to act.

anchor: touching Billy’s heart to the quick
note: To the quick: to the most sensitive part, deeply.

anchor: an expression which was as a crucifixion to behold
note: Crucifixion: execution on a cross, a figure for Billy’s agony.

anchor: so shapely and intellectual-looking a feature
note: Claggart’s forehead, which had seemed the sign of his intellect, takes the blow.
Fated: doomed, destined for ill.
Claggart’s body is limp and lifeless in their hands.

anchor: as impassive as the object at his feet
note: Impassive: showing no emotion, as still as the dead man.
Disciplinarian: one who enforces strict obedience to rules.
A state-room is a small private cabin, here in the rear of the ship.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “State-room”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: self-poised character of that grave sense and experience
note: Self-poised: calm and self-controlled, not easily shaken.
Revelation: the disclosure of something hidden.

anchor: the customary tests confirmed the Surgeon’s first glance
note: Surgeons then checked for breath and pulse, and used a mirror before the lips.

anchor: It is the divine judgement on Ananias
note: In Acts, Ananias lied to the apostles about money he had pledged and fell dead at Peter’s words. Vere sees Claggart as another liar struck dead.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Acts 5:1-5, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: Struck dead by an angel of God! Yet the angel must hang!
note: Vere cries that Billy was the angel of justice who killed a liar. Still, the law demands his death.
Incoherences: confused, disconnected statements that make no sense alone.
A drum-head court is a court-martial held on the spot, with a drum as the table.
Mordant means biting, sharp. Melville chose a name that suggests the officer’s sternness.
The Captain of Marines commanded the soldiers carried aboard a ship.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Marines”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000
